newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says no cigarettes during Super Bowl broadcast.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says no cigarettes during Super Bowl broadcast.

text.p: The Justice Department said Wednesday it has written to various parties involved in the Super Bowl to make sure that cigarette advertisements were not shown during the football game's broadcast.

The department said it contacted The News Corp 's Fox Television which will broadcast the game from the Superdome in New Orleans, the National Football League and Philip Morris, which has four Marlboro signs in the stadium.

Assistant Attorney General Frank Hunger said the Justice Department asked the various parties for their assistance in making sure the federal law banning cigarette advertising was not violated during Sunday's broadcast.
"We have done our part in alerting them to the potential problem," he said in statement. "We certainly expect that they will do their part to comply with the law."

The Justice Department in 1995 reached an agreement with Philip Morris , the world's largest cigarette maker, and Madison Square Garden in New York to make sure cigarette advertisements were not broadcast during sports events.

Department officials said Philip Morris has made arrangements to make sure an end-zone Marlboro sign -- which was shown on television during the 1997 Sugar Bowl college football game -- will be taken down just for Sunday's game.
